Fehergyarmat Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Fehérgyarmat, Hungary

Not demolished. The older of two Jewish cemeteries in Fehérgyarmat, in use from 1867 until burials gradually shifted to the newer cemetery around the late 1910s; its newest tombstone dates to 1923. Jews settled in Fehérgyarmat from the second half of the 18th century after being invited to work the local estate, later developing the town's agricultural trade in jams and wool; by 1930, the community included 25 merchants, 30 artisans, 9 industrialists, 5 lawyers, and 3 doctors among others. Independent from Csenger's rabbinate after 1810, the community joined the Orthodox stream following 1868-69's Schism, and from 1885 oversaw surrounding villages' rabbinates. Rabbi Shmuel David Halevi Jungreiss founded the local yeshiva (1868-1893), succeeded by Rabbi Yaakov Jungreis until the community's destruction. During Hungary's 1919-21 'White Terror,' an economic boycott and street attacks drove many to emigrate to the US and Canada. By 1944, the community numbered 708 with 108 children in its schools; German occupation that March saw full local cooperation in confining Jews, who were transferred to the Mátészalka Ghetto in April and deported to Auschwitz by month's end in May. Of 84 postwar survivors, most from forced labor camps, 23 later emigrated to Israel following its founding, with the rest eventually leaving as well.
